nodes.name: Chemical Reduction of FeCoPB (Mo₀)
nodes.procedure: 0.003 mol of mixed metal salts (FeCl₂·4H₂O and CoCl₂·6H₂O) and 0.009 mol of sodium hypophosphite (NaH₂PO₂·H₂O) were dissolved in deionized water. Afterward, 0.009 mol of sodium borohydride (NaBH₄) was dropwise added into the mixture using a constant-flow pump at a rate of 10 mL min⁻¹. The synthetic process was executed for 50 min under high-purity nitrogen protection with mechanical stirring at room temperature. The resultant precipitates were then washed with deionized water and ethanol in sequence for three times and collected by extraction filtration. All the samples were dried in vacuum at room temperature in 24 h for the subsequent experiments/characterizations.

nodes.characterization_summary: All FeCoMoPB samples (Mo0 to Mo10) exhibit broad diffuse peak at 44° indicating amorphous phase; Mo0 shows additional metal oxide peaks at 33° and 61° that diminish with increasing Mo content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b shows the structural characterization of the as-prepared FeCoMoPB samples. It was found that the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Mo0 sample exhibits three diffusive peaks at 33°, 44°, and 61°, respectively... When the Mo amount is increased from Mo0 to Mo7, the metal oxide peaks gradually become invisible and the Mo10 sample only presents a broad diffuse diffraction peak...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5 sample shows nanoplate morphology with average size ≈20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images in Figure 1c,d show a nanoplate morphology of the Mo5 sample with an average size of ≈20 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5 sample shows nanoplate morphology ≈20 nm with amorphous structure confirmed by broad diffuse rings in SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images in Figure 1c,d show a nanoplate morphology of the Mo5 sample with an average size of ≈20 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5 sample shows broad diffuse rings without lattice fringes in SAED confirming amorphous structure; inhomogeneous contrast indicates local atomic ordering at sub-nanoscale.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1e and inset present the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the Mo5 sample. Broad diffuse rings without lattice fringes are observed, corroborating its amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5 sample shows uniform distribution of Fe, Co, Mo, P, O with B enriched at outer layer of nanoplates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping results of Fe, Co, Mo, P, B, and O in the Mo5 amorphous nanoplate are acquired by the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0 shows only oxidized states Fe2+ (709.5 eV), Fe3+ (712.8 eV), Co2+ (781.1 eV); Mo5 shows additional metallic Fe0 (706.5 eV), Co0 (777.8 eV), Mo6+ (232.1, 235.5 eV), M-P (129.5 eV), M-B (188.2 eV), POx (133.1 eV), BOx (191.3 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is noteworthy that the Fe and Co elements only exhibit oxidized states of Fe2+ (709.5 eV), Fe3+ (712.8 eV), and Co2+ (781.1 eV) on the Mo0 sample, respectively, whereas Fe0 (706.5 eV) and Co0 (777.8 eV) peaks are clearly observed on the Mo5 sample...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5 specific surface area measured by BET is 6.1 times lower than FeCoMoB sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the specific surface area of the Mo5 sample measured by Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) method presents 6.1 times lower than that of the FeCoMoB sample (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Used Mo5 after 48h OER shows sheet-like and nanoplate structures maintaining amorphous nature in nanoplate regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To highlight the excellent stability of the Mo5 amorphous nanoplates, its structural variation after 48h OER is characterized by TEM (Figure 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Used Mo5 sheet-like structure shows nanocrystallization with FeOOH (111: 2.45Å, 220: 2.93Å, 110: 2.52Å), CoOOH, FeOOH (011: 2.47Å) at edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, the HRTEM images (Figure 4d,e) with the corresponding SAED pattern (Figure 4f) of the sheet-like structure present an obvious nanocrystallization behavior.

nodes.characterization_summary: Used Mo5 shows similar atomic distribution of Mo, Fe, Co, B, P, O compared to fresh sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping results of Mo, Fe, Co, B, P, and O for the used Mo5 sample present a similar atomic distribution compared with those of the as-prepared Mo5 sample...

nodes.characterization_summary: Used Mo5 after 48h OER shows sheet-like and nanoplate morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two typical morphologies of the used Mo5 sample including sheet-like and nanoplate structures are shown in Figure 4a,b, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Used Mo5 nanoplate maintains amorphous structure; sheet-like structure shows FeOOH nanocrystals (111: 2.45Å, 220: 2.93Å, 110: 2.52Å) and CoOOH/FeOOH (011: 2.47Å, 001: 2.37Å) at edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4c shows the HRTEM image of the selected area from the nanoplate structure, demonstrating the structure maintains in amorphous. However, the HRTEM images (Figure 4d,e)... Lattice space fringes of 2.45, 2.93, and 2.52Å which are in agreement with the (111), (220), and (110) planes of FeOOH crystalline phase...
